mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.2% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate cuts, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.22 in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior month's return (t-test p > 0.05), or the S&P 500 underperforms the risk-free rate by more than 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a month, the immediate effect is a steeper discount curve for future cash flows, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening in the policy rate cycle
failure_condition: In regimes where FEDFUNDS increases >0.25pp, the 60-day forward return is positive in >70% of instances (Rank IC > 0.5), or the 60-day IC is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index exceeding 0.3% signals wage inflation, prompting a preemptive equity premium and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >0.3% month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 100 instances where PAYEMS rises >0.3% monthly, the 5-day forward return is negative (IC < -0.05), or the IC is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in INDPRO manufacturing index below 50 (year-on-year) indicates weakening supply capacity, which elevates uncertainty and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 50 in the current month
failure_condition: In >40% of INDPRO < 50 events, the 20-day forward return is positive (IC > 0.1), or the IC is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST retail sales exceed 1% month-over-month for three consecutive months, it signals resilient consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 50 such HOUST >1% streaks, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (IC ≤ 0.0), or the IC is flat (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months, the labor market softness is interpreted as a risk-off signal, predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: In >60% of UNRATE < 3.5% events, the 5-day forward return is positive (IC > 0.05), or the IC is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 4.0% for 4 consecutive months), the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be positive due to lower borrowing costs and higher equity valuation multiples, unless inflation surprises persistently remain above 0.4%.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 4.0% for 4 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL < 0.4% over the same window
failure_condition: In >80% of easing regimes, the 20-day forward return is negative (IC < -0.1), or the inflation premium (CPIAUCSL - 2.5%) does not rise above 1% (p > 0.05).
